title: Bad restriction weight for bounded-width DNF
statement: Let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ Boolean variables whose terms each contain distinct variables, and suppose its width is at most $w$. Choose each coordinate restriction independently: leave it free with weight $\delta$, or fix it to either sign with weight $(1-\delta)/2$. Call a restriction bad when the restricted function is nonconstant. If $0\le\delta\le 1/3$, then the total weight of bad restrictions is at most $3\delta w$.
hypotheses_covered: $\varphi$ is a DNF formula on $n$ coordinates
each term has pairwise distinct literal indices (part of the term definition)
